To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) group fusion of similarity searching results can significantly improve the performance of similarity searching in cases where the actives have diverse scaffolds; and (b) turbo similarity searching can significantly improve the effectiveness of similarity searching, even in the case of structurally homogeneous actives, and it does not require the availability of multiple reference structures.

group fusion is effective for scaffold-hopping searches; group fusion is not useful for searches of structurally homogeneous sets of actives; and turbo similarity searching is more effective than conventional approaches for similarity searches.

(i) group fusion can enhance the effectiveness of scaffold-hopping similarity searches, (ii) turbo similarity searching is an effective method for ligand-based virtual screening that combines similarity searching and machine learning, and (iii) both techniques are notably more effective than standard similarity searching.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for ligand-based virtual screening.
developing new methods for ligand-based virtual screening that will be effective when the bioactivity data are incomplete or noisy.
the application of data fusion and machine learning techniques to the problem of similarity searching.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the fusion of results from similarity searching using multiple reference structures is the most effective way to search a chemical structure database for structurally diverse actives; turbo similarity searching using a single reference structure is the next most effective way; and conventional similarity searching, using a single reference or multiple reference structures, is the least effective way.

the two techniques described here, group fusion and turbo similarity searching, can be used to improve the performance of conventional similarity searches in the case of structurally diverse sets, but not in the case of sets of structurally similar compounds.
the fusion of similarity search results, using multiple reference structures, can significantly improve the effectiveness of scaffold-hopping searches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of multiple bioactive reference structures, in combination with the turbo approach, can provide a significant improvement in the effectiveness of ligand-based virtual screening.

, if the actives in a database are structurally diverse, group fusion and turbo similarity searching will be effective at finding new actives, and if the actives have a common scaffold, conventional similarity searching is more effective.

, when multiple bioactive reference structures are available, the most effective approach to ligand-based virtual screening is to use the group fusion technique described in this paper; when only a single bioactive structure is available, turbo similarity searching should be used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of multiple bioactive reference structures is likely to enhance the effectiveness of similarity searching.
the performance of similarity searching can be improved by using multiple reference structures and by combining the results of similarity searching with other techniques.
, in the context of similarity searching, it is possible to use the results from one search to improve the results of subsequent searches.
